question.text: At the centre of a fixed large circular coil of radius $\mathrm{R}$, a much smaller circular coil of radius $r$ is placed. The two coils are concentric and are in the same plane. The larger coil carries a current I. The smaller coil is set to rotate with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis along their common diameter. Calculate the emf induced in the smaller coil after a time $t$ of its start of rotation.

solution.text:
According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction,
$$
\begin{array}{r}
e=-\frac{d \phi}{d t} \text { and } \phi=B A \cos \omega t=B \pi r^2 \cos \omega t \\
\Rightarrow \quad e=-\frac{d}{d t}\left(\pi r^2 B \cos \omega t\right)=\pi r^2 B \sin \omega t(\omega) \\
\therefore e=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 R} \pi \omega r^2 \sin \omega t\left(\because B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 R}\right)
\end{array}
$$
